studies.label: Randomized lab experiment: product improvement followed by unassisted product invention

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 8, Method, Participants; analyzed arm counts are in Design on the same page and Table 4 on PDF p. 20
counts_source.quote: Outcomes reported below are based on data from 196 participants; one participant who failed to adhere to the experimental instructions was excluded from analyses.

arms.name: human-only
arms.description: Solved the 12-minute product improvement task independently with no other tabs or windows open, then solved the product invention task independently (PDF pp. 13-14).

arms.name: general-AI
arms.description: Could freely use ChatGPT-4 in a split-screen layout throughout the 12-minute product improvement task; instructed to use clear, detailed prompts and context. Then completed product invention without ChatGPT (PDF pp. 13-14).

arms.name: regulated-AI
arms.description: Think first, ChatGPT later: 3 minutes independently generating initial ideas, 6 minutes developing them with ChatGPT-4 as a brainstorming and feedback partner, then 3 minutes independently refining and submitting the best idea. Seven sample prompts were supplied and participants could use their own prompts. Then completed product invention without ChatGPT or sample prompts (PDF pp. 9 and 14; Appendix A, PDF pp. 34-35).

studies.task: Propose one creative improvement to a stuffed bunny, then independently invent and fully describe a fun, effective foreign-language vocabulary game for adults and university students (PDF p. 14; Appendices A-B, PDF pp. 33-35).

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT-4 (GPT-4 version of ChatGPT via the web interface through a ChatGPT Plus subscription; default parameters, with memory/model training switched off)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 13, Procedure; PDF p. 42, Reproducibility Note. The model release year and exact dated snapshot are not stated.

preregistration.where: No preregistration is reported in the full article. PDF p. 18 calls the outcome analyses confirmatory; the OSF link on PDF p. 41 is explicitly for data and analysis code.

estimates.outcome: Originality of the product improvement solution
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two trained, experienced experts, blind to condition, independently rated each participant's single solution on a 1-7 scale using the Consensual Assessment Technique. Responses were viewed in randomized order and judged relative to the response pool; the experts' ratings were averaged before analysis (PDF pp. 15-16). Originality means the uniqueness of the idea.

estimates.notes: Between-arm simple-effect comparison from the mixed learning-group by creative-task ANOVA; pairwise p-values are Bonferroni-corrected (PDF pp. 20 and 22). Arm SDs describe participant scores after averaging the expert ratings; they are not SDs across individual ratings (PDF pp. 15-16). The source sentence lists the general-AI versus human-only result first and the comparison of general-AI with regulated-AI second. Its printed d sign is retained; for the second result the negative sign matches regulated-AI minus general-AI.

open_items: The paper reports students who participated and the analyzed sample, but does not separately report total or per-arm counts at randomization, or the excluded participant's arm. Randomized counts remain null (PDF p. 8).

Regulated-AI final refinement is described as independent, but the paper does not state whether ChatGPT was closed or further use forbidden. Retain the screening form's with_ai classification for the product improvement task and flag this ambiguity (PDF pp. 9, 13-14, and 35).

The randomization method and whether lab sessions mixed conditions are not reported. Individual assignment is the paper's stated design; session allocation and any additional clustering cannot be confirmed (PDF pp. 8 and 12-13).
The exact GPT-4 snapshot, model release year, and data-collection dates are not stated; ai_tool.year remains null (PDF pp. 13 and 42).
The standardizing SD for the reported d values is not specified. Participant-level arm means and SDs are available for every extracted contrast (PDF pp. 15-16, 20, and 22).

Separate numeric SEs and confidence intervals for the main pairwise contrasts are not printed in the text or tables; Figure 2 shows standard-error bars, and Figure 3 contains mediation-model path intervals that were not read off the figures (PDF pp. 21 and 26).

Possible participant overlap with the earlier Qiu thesis is an unverified lead in the screening materials. The article does not identify the thesis and the form's sample_overlap supplies no confirmed shared sample; shared_sample remains null.
notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-10. Read the complete markdown conversion, including Appendices A-E and references, and checked the cited PDF pages with PyMuPDF text extraction. PDF page indices plus one match printed page numbers. All 18 estimates common to A and B are retained; the supplied diff contains one study-field difference and no estimate-field differences or one-sided estimates. All six screening outcomes and their three full-sample arm contrasts are represented. No additional eligible outcome or contrast was found. No across-people diversity measure, combined-AI versus control contrast, or overall-creativity composite is reported. Agreed-field audit: PDF p. 8 reports 196 analyzed participants and analyzed arm counts of human-only 64, general-AI 67, and regulated-AI 65, confirmed in Table 4 on PDF p. 20. The 197 students who participated are not explicitly a count at randomization; all randomized counts remain null. Two-arm totals are not printed and remain null. Individual participants were randomly assigned to fixed groups (PDF p. 8); successive outcomes on different tasks do not constitute randomized-order within-person contrasts, so within_person is null throughout. Participants attended a lab (PDF pp. 12-13). PDF pp. 9 and 14 identify product improvement as AI-assisted in both AI groups; its nine records are with_ai with outcome_with_ai true. The regulated group refined its final answer independently after ChatGPT interaction, but whether access was removed during that phase is unstated (PDF p. 14; Appendix A, PDF p. 35). Product invention was completed without ChatGPT or sample prompts (PDF p. 14); its nine records are after_ai with outcome_with_ai false. Both tasks occurred in the same session, so timing is immediate and the unprinted delay in days remains null. PDF pp. 15-16 define originality as uniqueness, usefulness as fulfilling the task goals, and elaboration as detail. These map to novelty, usefulness, and elaboration. Higher originality/usefulness means more_creative; higher elaboration is other, meaning more detailed, because the paper states that greater elaboration need not mean greater creativity. The two experts scored each participant's single solution, then averaged their ratings before analysis (PDF pp. 15-16), supporting unit = participant, sd_level = participant, and se_basis = participant. All arm means, SDs, Bonferroni-corrected pairwise p-values, and printed d values were independently checked on PDF pp. 20 and 22. The negative d signs for regulated-AI versus general-AI on intervention originality and usefulness are retained exactly as printed. The paper calls the scored outcomes primary but reports no preregistration (PDF p. 18; data/code availability on PDF p. 41). Under the codebook selection rules, general-AI versus human-only originality supplies the preferred ai_vs_bau record for each question. Regulated-AI versus general-AI is the proposed-versus-default ai_design contrast. Participants recur across outcomes and tasks, and contrasts share arms. The regulated protocol combines guidance, sample prompts, time allocation, and AI access; the absence of a matched regulated-human arm is acknowledged (PDF pp. 14, 29, and 32). No shared sample is confirmed by the article or screening form. Source quotes were matched to the cited PDF text, allowing only layout whitespace and discretionary line-break hyphenation normalization, and each is at most 40 words. Every populated numerical estimate field has exactly one source entry. Printed decimal precision is retained in numerical JSON tokens as well as quotes. No sample count, effect, standard deviation, standard error, or confidence interval was calculated from another statistic, and no value was read from a figure. No external data or supplement was used.
